would_leave_at: frame 2, when the cover repeats with no new information
first_impression: Useful niche recipe-fix idea, but it feels over-designed and a bit like an educational template rather than an appetizing human-made food post.
problems: The first frame has a decent quiz hook, but it is text-heavy and the food image is secondary, so it does not immediately feel delicious or urgent.
Frame 2 appears identical to frame 1, which wastes the opening seconds and makes the post feel slow.
Several frames use dense, small recipe text that is hard to read quickly on a phone.
The visual style relies heavily on boxes, badges, outlines and stock imagery, which makes it feel templated rather than personal.
The answer is useful, but the post takes a while to get there and the payoff is not very emotional or surprising.
The final source/disclaimer text is tiny and adds to the slightly institutional/ad-like feeling.
The food photography is labeled as licensed stock, which reduces trust and human warmth for a recipe post.
fixes: Remove the duplicate opening frame and get to the swap/answer faster.
Make the cover simpler: big food close-up, one headline, and larger A/B choices. Example: “Scaling tikka masala to 6? Don’t crowd the broiler.”
Use a real-looking broiler tray visual or quick before/after: crowded tray = steams, two uncrowded trays = chars properly.
Increase font size on recipe cards and cut copy to only the changed amounts and changed action.
Reduce the number of outlined boxes and badges; keep one consistent card style and let the food image breathe.
Move the key answer earlier: “Answer: use 2 sheets, one at a time — same 8–10 min.” Then explain why.
Replace stock imagery with an actual cooked dish/process shot if possible, even if imperfect; it will feel more trustworthy.
Make the save slide cleaner and more useful: one compact checklist with the 3 swaps plus the broiler rule, no tiny legal-looking block unless required.
